+"""Optional: a first iteration on the log schedule ends a logged interval, as any other does.
+
+Upstream ``training_log`` (Megatron-LM ``d3528a2``) does not reset its interval state after the
+first iteration of a run (``should_reset = not is_first_iteration``): the loss sums, the advanced /
+skipped / nan counters, the ``interval-time`` timer and the timers it logs. This is on purpose
+upstream, so the first line documents the start-up overhead. But when that first iteration is also
+a scheduled log iteration (``iteration % log_interval == 0``), it is counted again in the next
+logged interval: with ``log_interval`` 1 the second logged loss of a run (fresh or resumed) is the
+mean of two iterations. A resumed run then does not log the losses of the uninterrupted run.
+
+When enabled, this patch calls upstream with ``is_first_iteration=False`` for a first iteration
+that is on the log schedule. Upstream then logs it and resets everything itself, in the same way
+as for every other logged iteration (``interval-time`` with ``barrier=True``,
+``timers.log(..., reset=True)``, loss sums and counters). A first iteration off the log schedule is
+passed through unchanged (upstream logs it without a reset, as before). The flag is passed
+as ``False`` for the whole call, so the patch is correct only while upstream reads it in exactly
+the places listed in ``_UPSTREAM_FLAG_USES``; the patch reads ``training_log``'s source when it
+installs and raises if the uses differ (a Megatron bump that adds or changes one). Besides the
+reset and the log condition, the only other upstream
+use of the flag is the TensorBoard / WandB ``iteration-time`` write, which upstream skips for the
+first iteration (it includes the start-up overhead). The patch keeps that: during the call it hands
+upstream TensorBoard / WandB writers that drop only ``iteration-time``. The interval reset is not
+limited to stdout: every value upstream derives from the interval timer or sums changes for the
+logged interval after the first one, in stdout and in TensorBoard / WandB alike. That covers the
+loss and the interval timers, and also ``throughput``, ``iter-energy/gpu`` and ``power/gpu``. They
+then cover that interval only, without the first iteration and its start-up time.
+
+Scope: one model-independent switch, the module param ``log_reset_first_iteration`` (default
+off: upstream's logs). No model turns it on in code; a config does. The OLMo-3 example
+configs (``examples/megatron/configs/*/olmo_3_1025_7B-BF16-pretrain.yaml``) set it to ``true``,
+because a run started from them and resumed (``save``/``load`` given as overrides) at an
+iteration on the log schedule (a multiple of ``log_interval``) then logs the losses of the
+uninterrupted run. A run resumed off the schedule keeps upstream's behaviour: its first logged
+interval also counts the first iteration. Any model with the same setting logs the same way. A value that is not a switch is an error at
+patch time.
+
+The patch runs at priority 40, before ``megatron.training_log.unified_patch`` (default 50), which
+replaces ``training_log`` with a ``(*args, **kwargs)`` wrapper: this patch must bind the arguments
+with the signature of upstream ``training_log``. When the function it finds lacks
+``iteration`` / ``is_first_iteration`` (another wrapper came first, or upstream changed), the patch
+raises instead of silently not resetting. It also raises when the training module lacks
+``get_tensorboard_writer`` / ``get_wandb_writer``, since the start-up ``iteration-time`` could then
+reach TensorBoard / WandB. It wraps once (a second install is a no-op).
+
+``megatron.training.mlperf_logging`` (priority 15, so it runs first when enabled) replaces
+``training_log`` with a ``(*args, **kwargs)`` wrapper, silences Megatron's stdout log and sets the
+TensorBoard / WandB writers to None, and logs each step's own loss. There is then no interval log
+to reset: the patch logs that and does nothing, instead of refusing the run.
+"""
+
+import ast
+import inspect
+import textwrap
+
+from primus.core.patches import PatchContext, get_param, register_patch
+from primus.core.utils.arg_utils import parse_optional_switch
+from primus.core.utils.module_utils import log_rank_0
+
+PATCH_ID = "megatron.training_log.first_iteration_reset"
+# lower runs first: before megatron.training_log.unified_patch (default priority 50)
+PRIORITY = 40
+_NEEDED = ("iteration", "is_first_iteration")
+SWITCH = "log_reset_first_iteration"
+_MARK = "_primus_first_iteration_reset"
+# the attribute megatron.training.mlperf_logging sets on its training_log wrapper
+# (mlperf_logging_patches.py, ``_mlperf_training_log._primus_mlperf_logging_wrapper = True``)
+_MLPERF_MARK = "_primus_mlperf_logging_wrapper"
+
+
+# Where upstream training_log (Megatron-LM d3528a2) reads is_first_iteration: the enclosing
+# assignment, or the test of the enclosing if. The wrapper passes the flag as False for the whole
+# call and undoes only the iteration-time write; any other use would change silently.
+_UPSTREAM_FLAG_USES = (
+    "should_reset = not is_first_iteration",
+    "iteration % args.log_interval == 0 or is_first_iteration",
+    "args.log_timers_to_tensorboard and not is_first_iteration",
+)
+
+
+def flag_uses(fn) -> tuple:
+    """Where the function ``fn`` reads ``is_first_iteration``, as in ``_UPSTREAM_FLAG_USES``: per
+    read, the test of the enclosing ``if`` / ``while`` or else the enclosing statement (sorted).
+    Raises ``OSError`` / ``TypeError`` when the source cannot be read."""
+
+    tree = ast.parse(textwrap.dedent(inspect.getsource(fn)))
+    func = tree.body[0]
+    parents = {child: node for node in ast.walk(func) for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node)}
+    uses = []
+    for node in ast.walk(func):
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Name) and node.id == "is_first_iteration" and isinstance(node.ctx, ast.Load):
+            up = node
+            while not isinstance(up, ast.stmt):
+                up = parents[up]
+            if isinstance(up, (ast.If, ast.While)) and _contains(up.test, node):
+                uses.append(ast.unparse(up.test))
+            else:
+                uses.append(ast.unparse(up).splitlines()[0])
+    return tuple(sorted(uses))
+
+
+def expected_flag_uses() -> tuple:
+    """``_UPSTREAM_FLAG_USES`` in the form :func:`flag_uses` returns (``ast.unparse``, sorted)."""
+
+    return tuple(sorted(ast.unparse(ast.parse(u)).splitlines()[0] for u in _UPSTREAM_FLAG_USES))
+
+
+def _contains(tree, node) -> bool:
+
+    return any(n is node for n in ast.walk(tree))
+
+
+def _missing_in(sig) -> list:
+    """The parameters of ``_NEEDED`` that the signature ``sig`` lacks."""
+    return [name for name in _NEEDED if name not in sig.parameters]
+
+
+def reset_enabled(ctx) -> bool:
+    """The module param ``log_reset_first_iteration`` (a switch; another value raises); unset is
+    off, for every model, and so is a missing context (``ctx`` None)."""
+    if ctx is None:
+        return False
+    return parse_optional_switch(get_param(ctx, SWITCH, None), SWITCH)
+
+
+def reset_requested(ctx) -> bool:
+    """Patch condition, never raises (as ``checkpoint_path.routes_save``): a value that is not a
+    switch selects the patch, whose body raises the error inside the patch runner's per-patch
+    error handling (``[Patch] ... failed`` context, ``stop_on_error``). The switch is read by
+    :func:`reset_enabled` (the module param, with ``get_param``)."""
+    try:
+        return reset_enabled(ctx)
+    except ValueError:
+        return True
+
+
+_DROPPED_SCALAR = "iteration-time"
+
+
+class _TensorboardWithoutIterationTime:
+    """A TensorBoard writer that drops ``add_scalar("iteration-time", ...)``; the rest delegates."""
+
+    def __init__(self, writer):
+        self._writer = writer
+
+    def add_scalar(self, tag, *args, **kwargs):
+        if tag != _DROPPED_SCALAR:
+            return self._writer.add_scalar(tag, *args, **kwargs)
+        return None
+
+    def __getattr__(self, name):
+        return getattr(self._writer, name)
+
+
+class _WandbWithoutIterationTime:
+    """A WandB writer whose ``log`` drops the ``iteration-time`` key; the rest delegates."""
+
+    def __init__(self, writer):
+        self._writer = writer
+
+    def log(self, data, *args, **kwargs):
+        if isinstance(data, dict) and _DROPPED_SCALAR in data:
+            data = {k: v for k, v in data.items() if k != _DROPPED_SCALAR}
+            if not data:
+                return None
+        return self._writer.log(data, *args, **kwargs)
+
+    def __getattr__(self, name):
+        return getattr(self._writer, name)
+
+
+_WRITER_GETTERS = ("get_tensorboard_writer", "get_wandb_writer")
+
+
+def _call_without_iteration_time(fn, module, args, kwargs):
+    """``fn(*args, **kwargs)`` with ``module.get_tensorboard_writer`` / ``get_wandb_writer``
+    returning writers that drop ``iteration-time`` (restored afterwards). ``module`` None (no
+    writers to filter, e.g. a test stand-in): a plain call. ``wrap_training_log`` has checked
+    that a given module has both getters."""
+    if module is None:
+        return fn(*args, **kwargs)
+    saved = {n: getattr(module, n) for n in _WRITER_GETTERS}
+
+    def tensorboard():
+        writer = saved["get_tensorboard_writer"]()
+        return _TensorboardWithoutIterationTime(writer) if writer else writer
+
+    def wandb():
+        writer = saved["get_wandb_writer"]()
+        return _WandbWithoutIterationTime(writer) if writer else writer
+
+    module.get_tensorboard_writer, module.get_wandb_writer = tensorboard, wandb
+    try:
+        return fn(*args, **kwargs)
+    finally:
+        for n, v in saved.items():
+            setattr(module, n, v)
+
+
+def wrap_training_log(original_fn, get_megatron_args, module=None, check_uses=False):
+    """``training_log`` that passes ``is_first_iteration=False`` for a first iteration on the log
+    schedule, so upstream resets the interval as for any other logged iteration. For that call the
+    writers that ``module`` (upstream's training module) hands out drop ``iteration-time``, as
+    upstream does for a first iteration. Returns ``original_fn`` if it is already wrapped; raises
+    ``RuntimeError`` if its signature lacks the parameters the patch reads, or if ``module`` lacks
+    the writer getters (the start-up iteration-time could then reach TensorBoard / WandB), or if
+    ``check_uses`` (the patch sets it) and ``original_fn`` reads ``is_first_iteration`` elsewhere
+    than in ``_UPSTREAM_FLAG_USES``."""
+    if getattr(original_fn, _MARK, False):
+        return original_fn
+    if module is not None and not all(hasattr(module, n) for n in _WRITER_GETTERS):
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"[Patch:{PATCH_ID}] the training module lacks {list(_WRITER_GETTERS)}; cannot keep the "
+            f"first iteration-time out of TensorBoard / WandB. Set {SWITCH}: false to run without it."
+        )
+    sig = inspect.signature(original_fn, follow_wrapped=False)
+    missing = _missing_in(sig)
+    if missing:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"[Patch:{PATCH_ID}] training_log lacks parameter(s) {missing} (another wrapper ran "
+            f"first, or upstream changed); cannot reset the first logged interval. Set "
+            f"{SWITCH}: false to run without it."
+        )
+    if check_uses:
+        try:
+            uses = flag_uses(original_fn)
+        except (OSError, TypeError, SyntaxError) as e:
+            uses = f"unreadable source ({type(e).__name__}: {e})"
+        if uses != expected_flag_uses():
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"[Patch:{PATCH_ID}] training_log reads is_first_iteration in {uses}, not in the "
+                f"places this patch is written for {sorted(_UPSTREAM_FLAG_USES)} (upstream changed); "
+                f"cannot pass is_first_iteration=False safely. Set {SWITCH}: false to run without it."
+            )
+
+    def training_log(*args, **kwargs):
+        bound = sig.bind(*args, **kwargs)
+        bound.apply_defaults()
+        call = bound.arguments
+        if call["is_first_iteration"] and call["iteration"] % get_megatron_args().log_interval == 0:
+            call["is_first_iteration"] = False
+            return _call_without_iteration_time(original_fn, module, bound.args, bound.kwargs)
+        return original_fn(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    setattr(training_log, _MARK, True)
+    training_log.__wrapped__ = original_fn
+    return training_log
+
+
+@register_patch(
+    PATCH_ID,
+    backend="megatron",
+    phase="before_train",
+    description="A first iteration on the log schedule resets the logged interval (log_reset_first_iteration).",
+    condition=reset_requested,
+    priority=PRIORITY,
+)
+def patch_training_log_first_iteration_reset(ctx: PatchContext):
+    # the condition (reset_requested) does not raise; a value that is not a switch raises here, and
+    # an off switch installs nothing, whoever calls the patch
+    if not reset_enabled(ctx):
+        return
+    import megatron.training.training as training_module
+    from megatron.training import get_args as get_megatron_args
+
+    original = training_module.training_log
+    if getattr(original, _MLPERF_MARK, False):
+        log_rank_0(
+            f"[Patch:{PATCH_ID}] MLPerf logging replaces Megatron's interval log; {SWITCH} has nothing "
+            "to reset and is not applied"
+        )
+        return
+    # owns "wrap once"; check_uses: upstream reads is_first_iteration only where the patch expects
+    wrapped = wrap_training_log(original, get_megatron_args, training_module, check_uses=True)
+    if wrapped is original:
+        return
+    training_module.training_log = wrapped
+    log_rank_0(f"[Patch:{PATCH_ID}] a first iteration on the log schedule resets the logged interval")

+    "false": False,

+    "no": False,

+    """An on/off setting: a bool, the int 0 / 1, or one of the strings true / false / yes / no /

+def _olmo3_bad_loss_report(stdout: str, train_iters: int, vocab_size: int | None = None) -> list[str]:
+    """Problems in Megatron's per-iteration lines (run with --log_interval 1, so one line per
+    iteration). Megatron prints 'lm loss' only when the interval average is > 0, so a NaN (or a
+    zero / negative) loss shows as a line *without* 'lm loss'; every line must have a finite,
+    positive one. Also refuses nonzero skipped / nan iteration counts and missing iterations.
+
+    With ``vocab_size``: a freshly initialised model predicts close to uniform, so the first loss
+    must be within 1.5 of ln(vocab_size) (a broken norm, scale or embedding moves it far away), and
+    no later loss may exceed the first by more than 0.5 (training must not diverge)."""
+    problems = []
+    lines = {}
+    for line in stdout.splitlines():
+        m = re.search(r"iteration\s+(\d+)/\s*(\d+)\s*\|", line)
+        if m and int(m.group(2)) == train_iters:
+            lines[int(m.group(1))] = line
+    missing = sorted(set(range(1, train_iters + 1)) - set(lines))
+    if missing:
+        problems.append(f"no iteration line for iterations {missing}")
+    for it, line in sorted(lines.items()):
+        m = re.search(r"lm loss:\s*(\S+)", line)
+        if m is None:
+            problems.append(f"iteration {it}: no 'lm loss' (NaN, inf or <= 0)")
+        else:
+            try:
+                value = float(m.group(1))
+            except ValueError:
+                value = float("nan")
+            if not (math.isfinite(value) and value > 0):
+                problems.append(f"iteration {it}: lm loss {m.group(1)!r}")
+        for what in ("nan", "skipped"):
+            c = re.search(rf"number of {what} iterations:\s*(\d+)", line)
+            if c is None or int(c.group(1)):
+                problems.append(
+                    f"iteration {it}: number of {what} iterations: {c.group(1) if c else 'missing'}"
+                )
+    if vocab_size and not problems:
+        losses = [float(re.search(r"lm loss:\s*(\S+)", lines[it]).group(1)) for it in sorted(lines)]
+        expected = math.log(vocab_size)
+        if abs(losses[0] - expected) > 1.5:
+            problems.append(f"first lm loss {losses[0]} is not near ln(vocab_size) = {expected:.2f}")
+        if max(losses) > losses[0] + 0.5:
+            problems.append(f"lm loss rises from {losses[0]} to {max(losses)}")
+    return problems

+
+import importlib.util
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+
+_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[5] / "primus/backends/megatron/core/models/olmo3/olmo3_validation.py"
+_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("_olmo3_validation_pure", _PATH)
+olmo3_validation = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
+_spec.loader.exec_module(olmo3_validation)
+
+check_olmo3_unsupported = olmo3_validation.check_olmo3_unsupported

+
+def test_enum_keys_refuse_none_strings_but_unset_values_stay_unset():
+    """For the enum keys Megatron compares exactly, the strings none / null / ~ are values, not
+    "unset" (position_embedding_type: none is "no position embedding"), so they are refused. Only
+    Python None passes. Keys whose readers treat null as unset (window_attn_skip_freq) still do."""
+
+    for key, bad in (
+        ("position_embedding_type", "none"),
+        ("position_embedding_type", "null"),
+        ("normalization", "None"),
+        ("normalization", "NONE"),
+        ("softmax_type", "none"),
+        ("softmax_type", "null"),
+        ("transformer_impl", "null"),
+        ("transformer_impl", "~"),
+    ):
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=key):
+            check_olmo3_unsupported(SimpleNamespace(**{key: bad}))
+    for key, good in (
+        ("position_embedding_type", "rope"),
+        ("normalization", "RMSNorm"),
+        ("softmax_type", "vanilla"),
+        ("transformer_impl", "transformer_engine"),
+    ):
+        check_olmo3_unsupported(SimpleNamespace(**{key: good}))
+        check_olmo3_unsupported(SimpleNamespace(**{key: None}))
+
+
+def test_skip_freq_messages():
+    """A negative int gets the >= 2 message, not a parse error."""
+
+    for bad in (-4, "-4", " -4 "):
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="must be >= 2"):
+            parse_olmo3_skip_freq(bad, 8)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="cannot parse"):
+        parse_olmo3_skip_freq("[1,0]**2", 4)
+
+
+def test_skip_freq_parser_is_fast_and_safe():
+    import time
+
+    t0 = time.monotonic()
+    for bad in ("[1]*10**10", "[1]*" + "9" * 4000, "(" * 2000 + ")" * 2000, "[1]*99999*99999"):
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="window_attn_skip_freq"):
+            parse_olmo3_skip_freq(bad, 4)
+    # generous bound: only an exponential blow-up (a real string evaluation) can exceed it
+    assert time.monotonic() - t0 < 10.0
+
+
+def test_window_form_spelling_is_one_rule():
+    """'HF' / ' megatron ' read the same in the window reader and the refusal table."""
+
+    for form, ws in (("HF", [4096, 0]), (" megatron ", [4095, 0])):
+        assert olmo3_window_from_settings(ws, None, form) == ((4095, 0), 4096)

+"""megatron.args.checkpoint_path and its model-independent keep_absolute_save_path switch."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+
+
+def test_generic_checkpoint_path_keeps_an_absolute_save_when_asked():
+    """megatron.args.checkpoint_path moves ``save`` to ``<exp_root>/checkpoints``; with the
+    model-independent switch keep_absolute_save_path and an absolute ``save`` the patch does not run
+    (its condition), so a run with ``load`` at the same path finds it. A relative save, or the
+    switch off or unset (the same unset values as log_reset_first_iteration), keeps the Primus
+    location. The switch on with a save that is not absolute is refused. No model-specific save patch exists.
+    """
+    from primus.backends.megatron.patches.args import checkpoint_path_patches as cp
+    from primus.core.patches.patch_registry import PatchRegistry
+
+    def run(save, model_type="gpt", **params):
+        backend = SimpleNamespace(save=save)
+        mc = SimpleNamespace(params=SimpleNamespace(model_type=model_type, save=save, **params))
+        ctx = SimpleNamespace(
+            extra={
+                "backend_args": backend,
+                "module_config": mc,
+                "primus_config": SimpleNamespace(exp_root_path="/exp"),
+            }
+        )
+        if cp.routes_save(ctx):
+            cp.patch_checkpoint_path(ctx)
+        return backend.save
+
+    assert run("/tmp/ckpt") == "/exp/checkpoints"  # unchanged default, every model
+    assert run("/tmp/ckpt", model_type="olmo3") == "/exp/checkpoints"
+    for model_type in ("gpt", "olmo3"):
+        assert run("/tmp/ckpt", model_type, keep_absolute_save_path=True) == "/tmp/ckpt"
+        assert run("/tmp/ckpt", model_type, keep_absolute_save_path="off") == "/exp/checkpoints"
+    for unset in (None, "", "null", "~"):
+        assert run("/tmp/ckpt", keep_absolute_save_path=unset) == "/exp/checkpoints"
+    for relative in ("ckpt", "~/ckpt"):  # the opt-in cannot be honoured: refused, not rerouted
+        assert run(relative) == "/exp/checkpoints"
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="not an absolute path"):
+            run(relative, keep_absolute_save_path=True)
+    from pathlib import Path
+
+    assert run(Path("/tmp/ckpt"), keep_absolute_save_path=True) == Path("/tmp/ckpt")
+    assert run(None, keep_absolute_save_path=True) is None  # save: null still opts out of saving
+    assert run(None) is None
+    for save in (None, "/tmp/ckpt", "ckpt"):  # an unreadable switch is refused whatever the save
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="keep_absolute_save_path"):
+            run(save, keep_absolute_save_path="bogus")
+    # backend_args.save None is the opt-out even if the module param names an absolute path: the
+    # condition does not skip the patch, so its opt-out message runs and nothing is saved
+    backend = SimpleNamespace(save=None)
+    ctx = SimpleNamespace(
+        extra={
+            "backend_args": backend,
+            "module_config": SimpleNamespace(
+                params=SimpleNamespace(save="/ckpt", keep_absolute_save_path=True)
+            ),
+            "primus_config": SimpleNamespace(exp_root_path="/exp"),
+        }
+    )
+    assert cp.routes_save(ctx)
+    cp.patch_checkpoint_path(ctx)
+    assert backend.save is None
+    # an unreadable switch value: the condition does not raise (patch selection goes on); the
+    # patch body refuses it
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="keep_absolute_save_path"):
+        run("/tmp/ckpt", keep_absolute_save_path="maybe")
+    assert PatchRegistry.get("megatron.olmo3.save_path") is None
+
+
+def test_routed_save_hint_only_for_an_absolute_save(monkeypatch):
+    """The WARN suggests keep_absolute_save_path only for an absolute save; with a relative save the
+    switch would refuse the run, so no hint."""
+    from primus.backends.megatron.patches.args import checkpoint_path_patches as cp
+
+    logs = []
+    monkeypatch.setattr(cp, "log_rank_0", logs.append)
+
+    def warn(save):
+        logs.clear()
+        ctx = SimpleNamespace(
+            extra={
+                "backend_args": SimpleNamespace(save=save),
+                "module_config": SimpleNamespace(params=SimpleNamespace(save=save)),
+                "primus_config": SimpleNamespace(exp_root_path="/exp"),
+            }
+        )
+        cp.patch_checkpoint_path(ctx)
+        return next(m for m in logs if "[WARN]" in m)
+
+    assert "keep_absolute_save_path: true" in warn("/tmp/ckpt")
+    assert "keep_absolute_save_path" not in warn("ckpt")
+
+
+def test_save_switch_and_reset_switch_read_unset_alike():
+    """keep_absolute_save_path and log_reset_first_iteration use one unset rule (is_unset)."""
+    from primus.backends.megatron.patches.args.checkpoint_path_patches import (
+        keep_absolute_save,
+    )
+    from primus.backends.megatron.patches.training_log import (
+        first_iteration_reset_patches as fr,
+    )
+
+    for value in (None, "", "null", "~", True, "true", False, "off"):
+        ctx = SimpleNamespace(
+            extra={
+                "module_config": SimpleNamespace(
+                    params=SimpleNamespace(keep_absolute_save_path=value, log_reset_first_iteration=value)
+                )
+            }
+        )
+        assert keep_absolute_save(ctx) is fr.reset_enabled(ctx), value

+"""native_convert_common.fuse_qkv: the mcore linear_qkv layout shared by the Llama, Qwen3 and
+OLMo-3 converters."""
+
+import pytest

+torch = pytest.importorskip("torch")

+def _labelled(nh, ng, hdim, hidden):
+    """q / k / v weights whose every value names its row: q row r is r, k row r is 1000 + r,
+    v row r is 2000 + r (constant along the hidden dimension)."""
+
+    def rows(n, base):
+        return (base + torch.arange(n, dtype=torch.float64)).unsqueeze(1).expand(n, hidden).clone()
+
+    return rows(nh * hdim, 0), rows(ng * hdim, 1000), rows(ng * hdim, 2000)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("nh, ng, hdim, hidden", [(8, 2, 4, 16), (4, 4, 8, 32), (6, 1, 2, 12), (6, 3, 4, 10)])
+def test_fuse_qkv_groups_query_heads_then_key_then_value(nh, ng, hdim, hidden):
+    """The fused rows, read back by their labels: group g holds the query rows of its nh / ng heads,
+    then its key rows, then its value rows (an independent oracle, no reshape)."""
+    from primus.backends.megatron.checkpoint.native_convert_common import fuse_qkv
+
+    q, k, v = _labelled(nh, ng, hdim, hidden)
+    fused = fuse_qkv(q, k, v, nh, ng, hdim, hidden)
+    assert fused.shape == ((nh + 2 * ng) * hdim, hidden)
+    assert torch.equal(fused, fused[:, :1].expand_as(fused))  # rows are kept whole
+    per = nh // ng
+    want = []
+    for grp in range(ng):
+        want += list(range(grp * per * hdim, (grp + 1) * per * hdim))
+        want += [1000 + r for r in range(grp * hdim, (grp + 1) * hdim)]
+        want += [2000 + r for r in range(grp * hdim, (grp + 1) * hdim)]
+    assert fused[:, 0].long().tolist() == want
+

+def test_fuse_qkv_refuses_head_counts(nh, ng):
+    from primus.backends.megatron.checkpoint.native_convert_common import fuse_qkv
+
+    q, k, v = _labelled(4, 2, 2, 8)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="positive multiple"):
+        fuse_qkv(q, k, v, nh, ng, 2, 8)

+def test_fuse_qkv_refuses_a_transposed_or_mis_sized_weight():
+    """GQA with non-square weights (nh * hdim != hidden, ng * hdim != hidden): a weight in the
+    nn.Linear [in, out] orientation (a real transpose) or with a wrong size is refused with the
+    expected shape, not reshaped into scrambled rows."""
+    from primus.backends.megatron.checkpoint.native_convert_common import fuse_qkv
+

+def _upstream_training_log(record):
+    """A stand-in with upstream's parameters that records how it was called."""
+
+    def training_log(
+        loss_dict,
+        total_loss_dict,
+        learning_rate,
+        iteration,
+        loss_scale,
+        report_memory_flag,
+        skipped_iter,
+        grad_norm,
+        params_norm,
+        num_zeros_in_grad,
+        max_attention_logit,
+        pg_collection=None,
+        is_first_iteration=False,

+

+def test_first_iteration_reset_hands_a_scheduled_first_iteration_to_upstreams_reset():
+    """A first iteration on the log schedule reaches upstream as a regular logged iteration
+    (is_first_iteration=False), so upstream resets the loss sums, counters, interval-time
+    (barrier=True) and the logged timers itself. Off the schedule, or not the first iteration, the
+    call is unchanged; positional and keyword calls bind the same way."""
+    from primus.backends.megatron.patches.training_log import (
+        first_iteration_reset_patches as m,
+    )
+
+    seen = []
+    args = SimpleNamespace(log_interval=1)
+    wrapped = m.wrap_training_log(_upstream_training_log(seen), lambda: args)
+    common = ({}, {}, 0.1)
+    rest = (1.0, "flag", 0, None, None, None, None)
+    assert wrapped(*common, 5, *rest, is_first_iteration=True) == "flag"
+    assert wrapped(*common, 5, *rest, None, True) == "flag"  # positional
+    assert wrapped(*common, 6, *rest) == "flag"
+    args.log_interval = 10
+    wrapped(*common, 5, *rest, is_first_iteration=True)  # not a log iteration: upstream decides
+    assert seen == [(5, False), (5, False), (6, False), (5, True)]
+    assert m.wrap_training_log(wrapped, None) is wrapped
+
+
+def test_first_iteration_reset_keeps_iteration_time_out_of_tensorboard_and_wandb():
+    """Upstream does not write iteration-time (it includes the start-up overhead) to TensorBoard /
+    WandB for the first iteration. With the reset the flag reaches upstream as False, so for that
+    call the writers drop iteration-time only; other scalars and later iterations are unchanged,
+    and the module's getters are restored."""
+    from primus.backends.megatron.patches.training_log import (
+        first_iteration_reset_patches as m,
+    )
+
+    tb, wb = [], []
+    tb_writer = SimpleNamespace(add_scalar=lambda tag, v, it: tb.append(tag), flush=lambda: "f")
+    wb_writer = SimpleNamespace(log=lambda d, it: wb.append(sorted(d)))
+    get_tb, get_wb = (lambda: tb_writer), (lambda: wb_writer)
+    module = SimpleNamespace(get_tensorboard_writer=get_tb, get_wandb_writer=get_wb)
+
+    def upstream(iteration, is_first_iteration=False):
+        w, b = module.get_tensorboard_writer(), module.get_wandb_writer()
+        if not is_first_iteration:
+            w.add_scalar("iteration-time", 1.0, iteration)
+            b.log({"iteration-time": 1.0}, iteration)
+        w.add_scalar("lm loss", 2.0, iteration)
+        b.log({"lm loss": 2.0, "iteration-time": 1.0}, iteration)
+        assert w.flush() == "f"  # other attributes delegate
+
+    wrapped = m.wrap_training_log(upstream, lambda: SimpleNamespace(log_interval=1), module)
+    wrapped(1, is_first_iteration=True)
+    assert tb == ["lm loss"] and wb == [["lm loss"]]
+    assert module.get_tensorboard_writer is get_tb and module.get_wandb_writer is get_wb
+    tb.clear(), wb.clear()
+    wrapped(2)
+    assert tb == ["iteration-time", "lm loss"] and wb == [["iteration-time"], ["iteration-time", "lm loss"]]

+    assert m.reset_enabled(ctx(model_type="olmo3", log_reset_first_iteration=True)) is True
+    assert m.reset_enabled(ctx(model_type="gpt")) is False
+    assert m.reset_enabled(ctx(model_type="gpt", log_reset_first_iteration=None)) is False
+    assert m.reset_enabled(ctx(model_type="gpt", log_reset_first_iteration="on")) is True
+    assert m.reset_enabled(ctx(model_type="olmo3", log_reset_first_iteration="off")) is False
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        m.reset_enabled(ctx(model_type="olmo3", log_reset_first_iteration="maybe"))
+    # the patch condition never raises: a bad value selects the patch, whose body raises inside the
+    # patch runner's per-patch error handling
+    assert m.reset_requested(ctx(model_type="olmo3", log_reset_first_iteration="maybe")) is True
+    assert m.reset_requested(ctx(model_type="olmo3")) is False
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="log_reset_first_iteration"):
+        m.patch_training_log_first_iteration_reset(ctx(log_reset_first_iteration="maybe"))
+
+
+def test_first_iteration_reset_patch_installs_once_before_the_unified_wrapper(monkeypatch):
+    """The registered patch replaces megatron.training.training.training_log once (a second run is a
+    no-op), and runs before megatron.training_log.unified_patch in the same phase, which would hide
+    upstream's signature behind a (*args, **kwargs) wrapper."""
+    import sys
+
+    from primus.backends.megatron.patches.training_log import (
+        first_iteration_reset_patches as m,
+    )
+    from primus.core.patches.patch_registry import PatchRegistry
+
+    training_mod, _ = _install_fake_megatron_training(monkeypatch)
+    seen = []
+    upstream = _upstream_training_log(seen)
+    training_mod.training_log = upstream
+    # upstream training.py imports both writer getters from global_vars
+    monkeypatch.setattr(training_mod, "get_tensorboard_writer", lambda: None, raising=False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(training_mod, "get_wandb_writer", lambda: None, raising=False)
+    args = SimpleNamespace(log_interval=1)
+    training_pkg = sys.modules["megatron.training"]
+    monkeypatch.setattr(training_pkg, "get_args", lambda: args, raising=False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(m, "log_rank_0", lambda *a, **k: None)
+    # the stand-in has upstream's parameters, not its body: report upstream's flag uses for it
+    real_flag_uses = m.flag_uses
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        m,
+        "flag_uses",
+        lambda fn: m.expected_flag_uses() if fn is upstream else real_flag_uses(fn),
+    )
+
+    def ctx(value):
+        return SimpleNamespace(
+            extra={"module_config": SimpleNamespace(params=SimpleNamespace(log_reset_first_iteration=value))}
+        )
+
+    on = ctx(True)
+    # off (or unset): the body installs nothing, even when called without its condition
+    for off in (ctx(False), ctx(None), None):
+        m.patch_training_log_first_iteration_reset(off)
+        assert training_mod.training_log is upstream
+    m.patch_training_log_first_iteration_reset(on)
+    wrapped = training_mod.training_log
+    assert wrapped is not upstream and wrapped.__wrapped__ is upstream
+    m.patch_training_log_first_iteration_reset(on)
+    assert training_mod.training_log is wrapped
+    wrapped({}, {}, 0.1, 1, 1.0, False, 0, None, None, None, None, is_first_iteration=True)
+    assert seen == [(1, False)]
+
+    mine, unified = PatchRegistry.get(m.PATCH_ID), PatchRegistry.get("megatron.training_log.unified_patch")
+    assert mine is not None and unified is not None
+    assert mine.phase == unified.phase and mine.priority < unified.priority
+
+    training_mod.training_log = lambda *a, **k: None  # a wrapper came first: fail loudly
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="lacks parameter"):
+        m.patch_training_log_first_iteration_reset(on)
+
+    # a functools.wraps (*args, **kwargs) wrapper does not pass the check through __wrapped__
+    import functools
+
+    @functools.wraps(upstream)
+    def opaque(*a, **k):
+        return upstream(*a, **k)
+
+    training_mod.training_log = opaque
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="lacks parameter"):
+        m.patch_training_log_first_iteration_reset(on)
+
+    # the MLPerf logging wrapper (priority 15, runs first) replaces the interval log: no-op, no error
+    def mlperf(*a, **k):
+        return upstream(*a, **k)
+
+    setattr(mlperf, m._MLPERF_MARK, True)
+    training_mod.training_log = mlperf
+    m.patch_training_log_first_iteration_reset(on)
+    assert training_mod.training_log is mlperf
+
+    # upstream with upstream's parameters but another use of the flag (a Megatron bump): refused
+    def changed(
+        loss_dict,
+        total_loss_dict,
+        learning_rate,
+        iteration,
+        loss_scale,
+        report_memory_flag,
+        skipped_iter,
+        grad_norm,
+        params_norm,
+        num_zeros_in_grad,
+        max_attention_logit,
+        pg_collection=None,
+        is_first_iteration=False,
+    ):
+        should_reset = not is_first_iteration
+        if is_first_iteration:
+            print("a new flag-gated behaviour")
+        return should_reset
+
+    training_mod.training_log = changed
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="reads is_first_iteration in"):
+        m.patch_training_log_first_iteration_reset(on)
+    assert training_mod.training_log is changed
+
+
+def test_first_iteration_reset_matches_upstream_flag_uses():
+    """The patch passes is_first_iteration=False for the whole upstream call and undoes only the
+    iteration-time write. Pins, on the pinned Megatron's real training_log, that the flag is read
+    in exactly the places the patch is written for (the patch checks the same at install)."""
+    training = pytest.importorskip("megatron.training.training")
+    from primus.backends.megatron.patches.training_log import (
+        first_iteration_reset_patches as m,
+    )
+
+    fn = training.training_log
+    while hasattr(fn, "__wrapped__"):
+        fn = fn.__wrapped__
+    assert m.flag_uses(fn) == m.expected_flag_uses()

+class TestSettingHelpers(unittest.TestCase):
+    """is_unset / parse_switch / as_int (used by the posttrain convert hook and the OLMo-3 code)."""
+
+    def test_is_unset(self):
+        for v in (None, "", " ", "null", "NULL", "~"):
+            self.assertTrue(is_unset(v), v)
+        # "none" is a value: a model or tokenizer path, or an enum value of some options
+        for v in ("x", "0", 0, False, "nil", [], "nul", "none", "None"):
+            self.assertFalse(is_unset(v), v)
+
+    def test_parse_optional_switch(self):
+        for v in (None, "", "null", "~"):
+            self.assertIs(parse_optional_switch(v, "k"), False, v)
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "k must be true or false"):
+            parse_optional_switch("none", "k")
+        self.assertIs(parse_optional_switch("on", "k"), True)
+        self.assertIs(parse_optional_switch(False, "k"), False)
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "k must be true or false"):
+            parse_optional_switch("maybe", "k")
+
+    def test_parse_switch(self):
+        for v in (True, 1, "true", "TRUE", " yes ", "On", "1", " 1 "):
+            self.assertIs(parse_switch(v, "k"), True)
+        for v in (False, 0, "false", "False", "no", "OFF", "0"):
+            self.assertIs(parse_switch(v, "k"), False)
+        # only the table: no number forms (a typo such as "+1" or "00" is refused, not read as 1 / 0)
+        bad = ("maybe", "", 2, 1.0, 0.0, -0.0, 0.5, "1.0", "0.0", "+1", "-0", "00", " 1.000 ", [], None)
+        for v in bad:
+            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "k must be true or false"):
+                parse_switch(v, "k")
+
+    def test_as_int(self):
+        self.assertEqual([as_int(v, "k") for v in (4, 4.0, "4", " -2 ", "+3", "4.0")], [4, 4, 4, -2, 3, 4])
+        self.assertEqual(as_int("4.00", "k"), 4)
+        for bad in (
+            True,
+            4.5,
+            1e20,
+            float("inf"),
+            "two",
+            "4.5",
+            "4.",
+            "\uff11\uff12",
+            "\u0663",
+            None,
+            "",
+            [4],
+        ):
+            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "k must be an integer"):
+                as_int(bad, "k")
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "unresolved"):
+            as_int("${TP:1}", "k")
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "k must be an integer"):
+            as_int("9" * 5000, "k")
+
